recap.narration_text: Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: passengers. after. personal limits. Driving behavior can be affected by personality, experience, social influences, road conditions and passengers. Defensive driving anticipates hazards instead of waiting to react after danger develops. A defensive driver recognizes personal limits and the limits of the vehicle.

Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: impair. reduce. Avoid driving. Stress and strong emotions can impair driving decisions and encourage impulsive risks. Predictable travel and steady lane position reduce uncertainty for other drivers. Avoid driving when emotional distress makes it difficult to handle the additional demands of traffic.

Keep these reminders connected to their full rules: unsafe. Unsafe. time. Aggressive driving includes tailgating, speeding, unsafe lane changes and failing to signal. Unsafe passing in front of a truck and repeated lane changes in truck blind spots can create severe danger. Allow enough trip time and avoid driving when angry or exhausted to reduce aggressive behavior.
